issues.legal_issue: An instrument chargeable with stamp duty cannot be admitted in evidence for a collateral purpose while it remains insufficiently stamped.
material_facts: An agreement for transfer of immovable property was tendered in a civil suit seeking recovery of the consideration paid, rather than enforcement of the transfer agreement.
The agreement provided for transfer of possession, and possession had been delivered to the purchaser.
The instrument had not been stamped with the duty applicable to a conveyance.
The transfer concerned land for which statutory permission was required and had been refused.
issues.conclusion: The agreement could not be admitted for the asserted collateral purpose while insufficiently stamped; the bar applies regardless of the purpose for which the instrument is tendered.
issues.legal_principle: Section 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 bars admission of a chargeable instrument that is not duly stamped for any purpose whatsoever, including a collateral purpose, unless the duty and applicable penalty are paid. The collateral-purpose proviso to Section 49 of the Registration Act, 1908 concerns non-registration and does not override the stamp-law bar. Ram Rattan v. Parmanand, AIR 1946 PC 51, supports the broad meaning of “for any purpose”; Sanjeeva Reddi v. Johanputra Reddi, AIR 1972 AP 373, and T. Bhaskar Rao v. T. Gabriel, AIR 1981 AP 175, explain the distinct effects of non-registration and non-stamping. Bondar Singh v. Nihal Singh, (2003) 4 SCC 161, concerned the Registration Act, not the Stamp Act, and therefore did not assist the appellant.

predicates.instrument_tendered_as_evidence_in_civil: A party offers an instrument as evidence in a civil proceeding.
predicates.instrument_chargeable_with_stamp_duty: The instrument is one on which stamp duty is payable.
predicates.instrument_duly_stamped: The instrument bears the stamp duty legally required for it.

issues.definition: When a chargeable instrument is tendered as evidence in a civil proceeding and is not duly stamped, it cannot be used for any purpose until the required duty and penalty are paid.

issues.legal_issue: An authority empowered to receive evidence must impound an instrument that appears not to be duly stamped when it is produced before that authority.
material_facts: The agreement was produced as evidence in a civil suit before a court authorized to receive evidence.
The agreement was chargeable with duty as a conveyance but had been insufficiently stamped.
The trial court directed that the instrument be impounded and required payment of the deficient duty and penalty.
issues.conclusion: The court was required to give effect to the statutory duty to impound the insufficiently stamped instrument, and the order was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 places a statutory obligation on persons authorized to receive evidence, including courts, to impound an instrument that appears not to be duly stamped. Under Section 35, an insufficiently stamped instrument may be admitted after payment of the deficient duty and the applicable penalty.

predicates.evidence_receiving_authority: A person or body has legal authority to receive evidence.
predicates.chargeable_instrument_produced_before_au: An instrument on which stamp duty is payable is produced before that authority.
predicates.instrument_appears_insufficiently_stampe: The instrument appears not to bear the full stamp duty required for it.

issues.definition: When a chargeable instrument appears insufficiently stamped and is produced before an authority empowered to receive evidence, that authority must impound it.

issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell immovable property under which possession is transferred without a conveyance is treated as a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes.
material_facts: The instrument was an agreement to sell immovable property.
The agreement provided for transfer of possession, and possession was delivered to the purchaser.
No conveyance was executed, and the agreement was tendered as evidence in a civil suit.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was deemed to be a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes and was chargeable with the duty applicable to a conveyance.
issues.legal_principle: The explanation to Article 23 of Schedule IA of the Stamp Act, as amended by the Madhya Pradesh Act No. 19 of 1989, creates a legal fiction under which an agreement to sell immovable property accompanied by transfer of possession without execution of a conveyance is treated as a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes.

predicates.agreement_to_sell_immovable_property: The parties made an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.possession_transferred_under_agreement: The seller transferred possession of the property to the purchaser under the agreement.
predicates.no_conveyance_executed: The parties did not execute a conveyance for the property.

issues.definition: An agreement to sell immovable property under which possession is transferred, without a conveyance being executed, is treated as a conveyance for stamp-duty purposes.
